title: Inference optimization and profiling
promotion_reason: mean latency still exceeds the baseline by more than the gate's 20% slack; the only configuration that passes destroys detection entirely
edge_note: No Jetson or N100 was available. Every latency figure below is Apple M4 Max and must not be read as production Edge performance.

baseline.note: stock COCO-pretrained yolox-tiny 0.1.1-rc0 installed in the model zoo

baseline_reproduction.conclusion: absolute figures differ from Colab because the CPU differs; the ratio reproduces the rejection. The ±37% spread makes the existing methodology unusable as an optimization target, which is why a steady-state profiler was added.

cold_start_vs_steady_state.method: profiling.profile_inference, candidate 640, default threads, warmup=20, runs=200
cold_start_vs_steady_state.note: the first call is faster than the steady mean, which is the opposite of a normal cold start and was the clue that thread oversubscription, not warmup, drove the variance

pytorch_vs_onnx.method: identical fixed-seed 1x3x640x640 tensor, batch 1, 2 threads on both, warmup 20, runs 100

fp16.reason: onnxconverter-common is not in the workspace, and the CPU execution provider — the one the promotion gate benchmarks — does not accelerate FP16; it converts back to FP32 for compute. FP16 is the right lever for TensorRT on Jetson and must be measured there, not inferred from a Mac.

resolution_study.method: same checkpoint re-exported at each size (torch/onnxruntime parity validated at 1e-4); latency runs=150 intra_op=2; accuracy over the full 3692-image test split
resolution_study.conclusion: Lowering input resolution is not available. The weights were trained at 640 and the anchor-free head's scale priors travel with that; re-exporting the same weights at 416 does not retrain them and detection collapses to zero. 416 passes the latency gate exactly (1.00x) and detects nothing — the precise trap section 7 exists to prevent.

harness_validation.note: close enough to confirm the evaluation path is sound. The small difference is expected: the checkpoint handed back is epoch 13 of a 30-epoch config, not necessarily the weights that produced the Sprint 20 report.

defects_found.summary: Guardian's own checkpoints never loaded. Training saves OfficialYoloxWrapper.state_dict() with a yolox_model. prefix; load_into() received the bare YOLOX module, so none of the 462 tensors matched (missing=388, unexpected=462) and load_state_dict(strict=False) reported it only to the log.
defects_found.impact: any model.checkpoint in a config loaded as noise and detected nothing; upstream COCO checkpoints are bare so the defect stayed invisible
defects_found.unaffected: train resume, which torch.loads last.pt directly

defects_found.summary: load_into() dropped the head whenever num_classes != 80 — a property of the model being built, not of the checkpoint — discarding the trained head of any Guardian checkpoint.
compare.benchmark_onnx (30 runs, 5 warmups, ORT default threads) spread ±37% across identical repeats, so no 20% improvement is detectable through it.
defects_found.status: worked around by a steady-state profiler; the gate's own benchmark is unchanged

rejected_optimizations.reason: not accelerated by the CPU execution provider the gate benchmarks
all four levels fall inside measurement noise
no effect; the graph has no parallel branches to schedule
3.5x faster but Apple-only; the Edge targets are Jetson and N100, where the equivalent levers are TensorRT and OpenVINO and must be measured there

accepted_optimization.change: intra_op_num_threads = 2 on the CPU execution provider
accepted_optimization.accuracy_impact: none — a session option changes no numerics
accepted_optimization.reproducibility_impact: relative spread falls from 0.326 to 0.067, which is what makes the benchmark usable at all
accepted_optimization.why_it_does_not_pass_the_gate: the gate is a ratio and both models speed up, so 2.11x becomes 1.92x against a 1.20x allowance
accepted_optimization.note: measured on a 14-core heterogeneous Apple CPU. The optimal thread count is a property of the host, so this must be re-measured on the Edge target rather than hardcoded from here.

not_measured.item: full pipeline component breakdown (capture, preprocess, tensor copy, inference, postprocess, NMS, tracking)
not_measured.reason: StageTimer is built and tested for it, but the end-to-end pipeline run was not wired. The decisive part of section 3 was established regardless: the gate's number is model inference only, with no capture, preprocessing, NMS or tracking in it, so no work on those stages can move it.

recommendation: Do not promote. The candidate cannot be made to fit this gate by optimization, and cannot be shrunk by resolution without destroying it. The gate currently compares a 640 candidate against a 416 baseline — 2.37x the compute by construction — so the comparison itself should go to architecture review before any further optimization work: either re-baseline at matched resolution, or move the latency budget onto real Edge hardware where an accelerated execution provider is the actual lever.
